answer: Give each new identity a spiral of rising stakes: it begins on tiny, logged jobs, and only after unrelated peers verify each job does its escrow limit grow. A shale bed of cheap fake accounts can copy the first rung, but it cannot forge the accumulated cross-checked history behind the later rungs, so fresh identities stall at the bottom. Random audits of old work then burn the escrow of any identity whose history unravels, and one independent raven auditor with no stake can trigger such an audit. Sybil cost then scales with proven history, not with how fast accounts can be created.
